label: meaningful
label_meaning: meaningful: built from the seller's own published schema

expected_schema.description: The 202 acceptance body. Every non-2xx answer is JSON { error: { code, message } } with code one of: invalid_request, invalid_source_url, source_too_large, ingest_failed, pipeline_error, rate_limited, daily_cap_exceeded, not_found, literal_path_template, gone, unknown_job, unauthorized, not_configured, unavailable - and, by the capture rule, a non-2xx response is never charged.

fundingSource.description: What paid for this acceptance: `x402` (the on-chain payment you signed), `credits` (your account's balance, when you sent a Bearer token) or `voucher` (a free retry). Stated back to you so a caller holding both a token and a wallet never has to guess which one it just spent.

status.description: `queued` for pull mode; `awaiting_upload` for upload mode (the job queues when your PUT completes).

statusUrl.description: Free, token-gated status endpoint for this job. Keep it: the token is the only proof of ownership and is not recoverable.

uploadExpiresAt.description: Upload mode only: deadline for the PUT. Past it the job becomes a terminal `error` with no refund.

uploadUrl.description: Upload mode only: PUT the raw bytes here before `uploadExpiresAt`. Keep it - this response is the ONLY place the upload token is handed out (the status route never repeats it), and it is not recoverable.

attribution.derived_from: the schema and example output the seller publicly lists there
attribution.status: unclaimed: the owner can claim or remove the matching listing on the discovery board
